title: 45-Day Identification Strategy
name: 45-Day Identification Strategy
metaDescription: Building a workable 45-day identification list for a Denver exchange, with backup candidates lined up before the relinquished property even closes.

sections.html: Forty-five days sounds like enough time until the relinquished property actually closes and the clock starts. In a Denver market where multifamily and industrial listings can go under contract inside a week, waiting until day one to start touring replacement property is how investors end up naming something they only half want.

sections.heading: Why the Clock Starts Before Most Investors Are Ready
sections.html: The identification period runs from the day the relinquished property closes, not from the day the investor decides to sell, and it does not pause for weekends, holidays, or a slow week of showings. In Denver, RiNo and LoDo multifamily buildings and industrial space along the I-70 corridor tend to move fast once they hit the market, sometimes with an accepted offer inside days. An investor who starts touring replacement candidates on day one of the window is already behind whoever wrote an offer on day one of the listing.

sections.heading: Building a Pre-Close Shortlist
sections.html: We start the search before the relinquished sale closes, not after, so the identification list is built from properties the investor has already toured, priced, and ranked. That shortlist gets checked against listing status daily once the closing date is set, since a candidate that looked available three weeks out can be under contract by the time the window opens. The goal is walking into day one of the 45-day period with a ranked list already in hand, not a blank page.

sections.heading: What Goes on the Working List
sections.html:
Every candidate on the pre-close shortlist gets tracked the same way.

  • Asking price and any known price movement
  • Estimated days until the listing could go under contract
  • Fit against the investor's replacement criteria
  • Backup ranking if the top choice falls through
  • Whether the identification will run under the three-property rule or the 200 percent cap

sections.heading: Front Range Growth Cuts Both Ways
sections.html: In-migration into the Front Range keeps demand steady across most asset classes, which is good for an investor selling and bad for one trying to buy on a deadline. A Denver Tech Center office building or a Cherry Creek retail space can draw multiple offers inside its first two weeks on market, and an investor working against day 45 does not have the leverage to wait out a bidding process. Having two or three ranked backups going into the window matters more here than in a slower market, because the top choice is genuinely at risk of going to someone else first.

sections.heading: How Many Candidates Actually Belong on the List
sections.html: Most Denver investors do better with two or three well-vetted candidates than with a long list of properties toured once and never priced properly. A shorter list built on real touring, real pricing checks, and real conversations with sellers holds up better under a tight deadline than a long list assembled quickly to pad out options. We push investors toward depth on a handful of candidates rather than breadth across a dozen properties nobody has actually walked through.

sections.heading: Handling a Slow Start on the Relinquished Sale
sections.html: Not every relinquished property sells on the timeline the investor expected, and a slower sale means less lead time to build the pre-close shortlist before the identification clock starts. When that happens, we compress the search timeline rather than skip steps, prioritizing property tours and pricing checks over broader market surveys, so the investor still walks into day one of the window with a workable list even if it is shorter than it would have been with more lead time.

sections.heading: Naming the List Correctly on Day 45
sections.html: The identification itself has to be in writing, signed by the investor, and delivered to the qualified intermediary or another party to the exchange before midnight on day 45, described specifically enough that there is no ambiguity about which property is meant. A verbal mention to a broker does not count, and neither does a property under discussion but not yet named in writing. We confirm the written identification is delivered and dated correctly, though the investor and their tax advisor make the final call on what goes on the list.

faqs.q: When does the 45-day identification clock actually start?
faqs.a: It starts on the day the relinquished property closes, not the day the investor lists it or decides to sell, and it runs on calendar days including weekends and holidays.

faqs.q: Why does Denver move faster than the identification window assumes?
faqs.a: RiNo, LoDo, and Denver Tech Center listings across most asset classes can go under contract inside one or two weeks, so a candidate that looks available in week one of the window may not be available by week three.

faqs.q: Can I change my identification list after it's submitted?
faqs.a: You can revise or add properties up until midnight on day 45, but nothing can be added or changed after that deadline regardless of what happens in the market.

faqs.q: Does a verbal conversation with a broker count as identification?
faqs.a: No. The identification has to be a written, signed description delivered to a party to the exchange, typically the qualified intermediary, before the day 45 deadline.

faqs.q: How many backup properties should be on the list?
faqs.a: Enough to survive one or two of the top choices falling through. In a fast-moving Denver market, a list with only one candidate leaves no room if that property goes under contract with someone else first.

faqs.q: Does the identification deadline change for a larger or unusual property?
faqs.a: No. The 45-day count is the same regardless of asset type or size, which is part of why a large industrial or multifamily search benefits from starting the pre-close shortlist as early as possible.
